spec: Find the longest contiguous substring of a string in which no character repeats. If there are multiple substrings of the same maximum length, return the one that starts earliest. An empty string returns an empty string.

Find the longest contiguous substring of a string that reads the same forwards and backwards. If multiple substrings tie for the maximum length, return the one that starts earliest in the string. An empty string returns an empty string.

Count the total number of contiguous substrings of a string that are palindromes, including single characters (each counted individually) and substrings that repeat as different occurrences. An empty string has zero palindromic substrings.

Remove all punctuation characters (such as periods, commas, exclamation points, and other symbols from the standard ASCII punctuation set) from a string, leaving letters, digits, and whitespace unchanged and in their original order.

Count the number of whitespace-separated words in a string whose first character is a vowel (a, e, i, o, or u), case-insensitive. Words starting with any other character, including punctuation, are not counted.
Count the number of distinct characters that appear in a string, treating uppercase and lowercase letters as different characters. An empty string has zero distinct characters.

Determine whether a string consists only of numeric digit characters (0-9) and contains at least one character. An empty string returns False, as does any string containing a letter, punctuation, whitespace, or a sign character.
Find the first character in a string, scanning from left to right, that appears more than once anywhere in the string. If no character repeats, or the string is empty, return None.

Determine whether the round-bracket parentheses characters '(' and ')' in a string are balanced, meaning every opening parenthesis has a matching closing parenthesis later in the string and they are properly nested. Any other characters in the string are ignored for this check.

Reverse the order of the vowel characters (a, e, i, o, u, in either uppercase or lowercase) within a string, leaving all other characters in their original positions. Each vowel keeps its own original case as it moves to its new position.

Determine whether a string is an isogram, meaning no letter appears more than once, ignoring case and ignoring any non-letter characters such as spaces or hyphens. An empty string, or a string with no letters, counts as an isogram.

Given a string of whitespace-separated words and a maximum line width, greedily arrange the words into a list of lines such that each line contains as many words as fit without exceeding the width (words on the same line separated by a single space), moving to a new line when the next word would not fit. A single word longer than the width occupies its own line unchanged.
visible_tests: assert word_wrap('the quick brown fox', 10) == ['the quick', 'brown fox']
assert word_wrap('a b c d e', 3) == ['a b', 'c d', 'e']

spec: Given a string of whitespace-separated words and a minimum length threshold, count how many words have a length strictly greater than the threshold. An empty or whitespace-only string has zero such words.

Determine whether a string is a valid identifier: it must be non-empty, its first character must be an ASCII letter or underscore, and every subsequent character must be an ASCII letter, digit, or underscore.
Extract all numeric digit characters from a string, in their original order, and return them concatenated as a string. If the string contains no digits, return an empty string.

Extract all alphabetic characters from a string, in their original order and preserving their original case, and return them concatenated as a string. If the string contains no letters, return an empty string.

Given a string, convert the character at each even index (0-based) to uppercase and the character at each odd index to lowercase, considering all characters (letters and non-letters) when counting index positions. Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by the case change but still occupy an index.
Given a string and a list of candidate suffix strings, determine whether the string ends with at least one of the suffixes in the list. If the list is empty, return False.

Count the number of sentences in a string, where sentences are separated by one or more of the characters '.', '!', or '?'. Empty segments (such as trailing punctuation or consecutive punctuation marks) must not be counted as sentences.
visible_tests: assert count_sentences('Hello. How are you? Fine!') == 3

spec: Determine whether a string is a palindrome when only its alphanumeric characters are considered, ignoring case and skipping all spaces and punctuation. An empty string, or a string with no alphanumeric characters, counts as a palindrome.
visible_tests: assert is_palindrome_ignore_non_alnum('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama') == True
assert is_palindrome_ignore_non_alnum('Was it a car or a cat I saw?') == True

spec: Interleave two strings character by character, alternating starting with the first string, and appending any leftover characters from the longer string at the end once the shorter one is exhausted.
Reverse the order of the digit characters within a string, leaving every non-digit character fixed in its original position. For example, 'a1b2c3' becomes 'a3b2c1'.

Determine whether a string fully matches a wildcard pattern, where '?' in the pattern matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters (including an empty sequence). All other characters in the pattern must match themselves exactly.

Given a string of whitespace-separated words, remove consecutive duplicate words (case-sensitive), keeping only the first occurrence of each run of identical adjacent words, and join the remaining words with a single space.
visible_tests: assert remove_repeated_words('the the cat sat') == 'the cat sat'
assert remove_repeated_words('a b c') == 'a b c'

spec: Find all starting indices at which a substring occurs within a string, including overlapping occurrences, in order from left to right. If the substring is empty, return an empty list.

Determine whether two strings are isomorphic, meaning there exists a one-to-one mapping from each character of the first string to a character of the second string that is consistent across every occurrence in both directions. Strings of different lengths are never isomorphic.

Count the number of positions in a string where two consecutive alphabetic characters differ in case (one uppercase and the other lowercase), scanning through the whole string. Pairs where either character is not alphabetic are not counted.

Convert a string to a simple leetspeak form by replacing, regardless of case, the letters a, e, i, o, s, and t with the digits 4, 3, 1, 0, 5, and 7 respectively. All other characters, including other letters, digits, punctuation and whitespace, remain unchanged.

Given a string of whitespace-separated words, reverse the characters of every word whose length is even, while leaving words of odd length unchanged, then join all words back together with single spaces.
visible_tests: assert reverse_words_with_even_length('this is a test') == 'siht si a tset'
assert reverse_words_with_even_length('a bb ccc dddd') == 'a bb ccc dddd'

spec: Remove every whitespace character (spaces, tabs, and newlines) from a string, leaving all other characters in their original relative order.
Determine whether a string has a balanced number of single-quote characters and a balanced (even) number of double-quote characters, meaning both counts must be even for the result to be True.

Compute the sum of all numeric digit characters found in a string, treating each digit character as its integer value. Non-digit characters are ignored. A string with no digits has a digit sum of zero.
Given a string of whitespace-separated words, count how many of the words are palindromes when compared case-insensitively (the word reads the same forwards and backwards ignoring letter case).

Given a list of words and a target word, return the subset of words from the list (in their original relative order) that are anagrams of the target word, meaning they contain the exact same letters with the same frequency, compared case-insensitively.

Given a string, consider only its alphabetic characters in order and determine the minimum number of individual letters whose case must be flipped so that the letters alternate between uppercase and lowercase. Since the alternation could start with either case, return the smaller of the two possible costs. A string with no letters requires zero changes.

Remove the character at a given zero-based index from a string and return the resulting string. If the index is negative or is greater than or equal to the length of the string, return the string unchanged.
Return the middle character of a string if its length is odd, or the two middle characters if its length is even. An empty string returns an empty string.

Given a string of numeric digit characters, count how many consecutive '0' characters appear at the very beginning of the string before the first non-zero digit or the end of the string. An empty string has zero leading zeros.

Given a string of whitespace-separated words, compute a dictionary mapping each distinct word length to the number of words in the string that have that length. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty dictionary.

Determine whether a string can be constructed by repeating some non-empty substring of it two or more times (e.g. 'abab' is formed by repeating 'ab' twice). An empty string is not considered to have a repeated substring pattern.
